senses.gloss: m. (νᾶνος, nanus, of Semitic origin, fr. נסס, cmp. ממל fr. מלל) dwarf; (adj.) puny, stumped.
units: <cite ref="Niddah 24b:68">Nidd. 24ᵇ</cite>, opp. <cite ref="A03026"><he>אָרוּךְ</he></cite>; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 9:24">Num. R. s. 9</cite>.

<cite ref="Berakhot 58b">Ber. 58ᵇ</cite> <he>נ׳</he> one whose limbs are too small for his body, opp. <cite ref="K00605"><he>כִּיפֵּחַ</he></cite>; Tosef. ib. VII (VI), 3 <cite ref="N00903"><he>ננוס</he></cite> ed. Zuck. (Var. <cite ref="N00907"><he>ננס</he></cite>); Y. ib. IX, 13ᵇ bot.; Tanḥ. ed. Bub., Pinḥas 1. Sifra Emor, Par. 3, ch. III; <cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 7:6">Bekh. VII, 6</cite> (<cite ref="Bekhorot 45b:8">45ᵇ</cite>, of animals and of men).
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:15:3">Cant. R. to II, 15</cite>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 65:11">Gen. R. s. 65</cite> <he>נ׳ שבננסים</he> a puny dwarf.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 137">Midr. Till. to Ps. CXXXVII</cite>; <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 31:1">Pesik. R. s. 31</cite> <he>הנ׳ הזה</he> that dwarf (Nebuchadnezzar); a. fr.—

<cite ref="Chullin 63a:2">Ḥull. 63ᵃ</cite> <he>וסימנך ננוס פסול</he> and thy sign (to remember that the small species of <cite ref="U01860"><he>שקיטנא</he></cite> is unclean) be, ‘the dwarf is unfit’ (for priesthood).—Pl. <he>נַנָּסִים</he>, <he>נַנָּסִין</he>. Cant. R. l. c.; Gen. R. l. c., v. supra.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 37">Pesik. R. s. 37</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 62">Yalk. ib. 62</cite> <he>כפתורים נ׳</he> Caphtorites (<cite ref="Genesis 10:14">Gen. X, 14</cite>) are dwarfs; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Tamid 3:5">Tam. III, 5</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Middot 3:5">Midd. III, 5</cite> <he>עמודים</he> .<he>נ׳</he> small columns.
